result.summary: Followed GIT_SETUP.md's standard (non-worktree) procedure from the primary checkout /home/tvolodi/letflow, which holds local main. git checkout main succeeded (already on main). git pull --ff-only origin main initially failed (exit 1) not because local main had diverged from origin's history -- it was 1 commit behind, strictly fast-forwardable -- but because two shared coordination files (handoffs/orchestrator.log, handoffs/registry.json) had uncommitted local edits from ORCH's own claim of this run, which Git refused to overwrite via ff-only merge. This is not the 'local main diverged' BLOCKER scenario GIT_SETUP.md's step 2 anticipates, so did not abort the run: stashed just those two files (git stash push -- handoffs/orchestrator.log handoffs/registry.json), re-ran git pull --ff-only origin main (now exited 0, fast-forwarded 25cb9b1 -> 9c18ab3), then git stash pop to restore ORCH's edits. The pop produced one append-only merge conflict in handoffs/orchestrator.log (both origin's incoming commit and the stashed local edit appended a new STOP/CLAIM log line at the same tail position); resolved by keeping both lines in chronological order (verified zero leftover conflict markers) and staging the file. handoffs/registry.json auto-merged cleanly. Created feature/WF03-ISS0029-20260818 from the now-updated main (git branch --list confirmed no stale branch from a prior aborted run, so no -D needed), verified via git branch --show-current, and pushed with git push -u origin feature/WF03-ISS0029-20260818 (exit 0, new branch on remote, upstream tracking set). All three GIT_SETUP.md acceptance criteria met. Note for ORCH: the previously-uncommitted ORCH coordination-log edits (orchestrator.log CLAIM entry, registry.json IN_PROGRESS entry for this run) are now staged on this feature branch rather than on main -- ORCH should account for that when it later records this run's own log/registry entries (likely needs a rebase-safe append or a direct main commit at run close, not a naive re-append).
